pull.title: fix(review): stop old /pathway markers replaying and let real CodeRabbit rounds carry
pull.body:
The PR D (#221) reviews left gaps in the CodeRabbit spend policy. An old /pathway marker could count again, real CodeRabbit rounds could not carry, and outside-diff findings went uncounted. This PR closes them, so READY asks for a paid review only when one is needed.

## What changed

- **review-router.mjs (C1):** the router saves the id of the /pathway marker it used, on its own comment line (`review-router-consumed id=N`). It ignores markers at or below that id. After a return to draft and a UI Ready click at the same head, the old marker no longer counts as a checkpoint. The router saves the highest fresh marker id, so an unused marker cannot replay. The state line keeps main's shape, so a rollback still parses it.
- **review-status.mjs (C2):** a clean round that left only the summary comment (PR 213 shape) is a carry source. So is a review with no "Actionable comments posted" sentence (PR 205 shape). Outside-diff findings now count in every CodeRabbit review body: PR 205 (2) and PR 221 (5) counted 0 before. A coverage marker of another kind rules a summary out. A new `--json` field, `coderabbitCarryBlockers`, says why a carry failed. It is empty when the carry did not run. Reason strings are unchanged.
- **cr-fix.mjs (C5):** cr-fix picks its range with the same `newestCodeRabbitRound` that READY uses, so its line matches the carry source. It names merge commits in the range on stderr. It stops with no CLI run when CodeRabbit already reviewed the head (PR 211 shape).
- **pr-review-loop.md:** the CodeRabbit #221 round 2 wording fixes, the new behaviour, and two accepted risks. First, the `CLI fix review` line in the editable PR body has the same trust as labels (Dave, 2026-10-30). Second, a router comment written before this change can let a stale marker count once.

## Evidence

Proof type: bugfix

RED: `node --test scripts/github/review-status.test.mjs scripts/github/review-router.test.mjs scripts/github/cr-fix.test.mjs` @ d4270286
```text
(this branch's test files run against main's sources at d4270286)
review-status + review-router: tests 376, pass 354, fail 22
not ok 125 - C1a (CLI): same head, undo then UI ready with only the old marker is not a checkpoint and the raise note stays
not ok 366 - C2a: a clean round of an earlier head that left only the summary comment (live PR 213 shape) is a carry source
not ok 1 - scripts\github\cr-fix.test.mjs (newestCodeRabbitRound and the new checks are missing)
```

GREEN: `node --test scripts/github/cr-paid.test.mjs scripts/github/review-status.test.mjs scripts/github/pr-loop-sync.test.mjs scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.test.mjs scripts/github/review-router.test.mjs scripts/github/pre-pr.test.mjs scripts/github/cr-fix.test.mjs scripts/mods/validate-mods.test.mjs scripts/rules/test/coderabbit-cli-content.test.mjs` @ ed913f7e
```text
node --test (8 files): tests 630, pass 630, fail 0
claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods: 1014 pass, 0 fail
npx vitest run (.claude/hooks): 109 files, 2916 passed (at 31d81af7; no hook source changed after)
context-budget-guard --repo: 23512 chars (budget 23516); ondemand-index-check OK; rule-router probe 139/139
```

Artifacts: `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-prdfu-red.txt` (main checkout). Review record: `.claudedocs/2026-10-30-pr-d-review.md` (local).

## Reviews before this PR opened

- The workflow fix stage (3 Sonnet krakens and 1 Opus check) found 6 problems in its own first pass. All are fixed, including a rollback hazard in the router state line.
- A pre-push Opus review found no major findings and 6 minor ones. Five are fixed. One is a follow-up (below).
- The pre-pr CodeRabbit CLI run on e58a59a4 found 2 major findings and 1 minor. All are fixed in c4bbe411. Live reads now count #221's 5 outside-diff findings and #205's 2.
- The second CLI run on c4bbe411 found 2 minor findings (one fail-open: a notice body could carry). Fixed in 8b69c3e1 (test C2h).

## CodeRabbit round 1 (8b69c3e1)

1 Major (summary edit history read one page; now an incomplete history is untrusted) and 1 Minor (a notice no longer adds outside-diff findings), both fixed test-first in 74962d04.

## Paid PR review policy (Dave, 2026-10-30), added after round 1

- `scripts/github/cr-paid.mjs`: `check` ALLOWs a paid round only at <= $5 per round, <= $15 per day across sessions (ledger `~/.claude/state/coderabbit-paid.jsonl`), fewer than 2 paid rounds per PR, and a fix of <= 30 lines with no added files; otherwise ESCALATE to Dave; read errors fail closed. `record` writes the ledger row.
- Rules: `pr-review-loop.md` section 'Paid PR reviews'; `coderabbit-cli.md`; the pr_watch rate-limit line points to `cr-paid check`. `cr-paid.mjs` joins `checkpoint.critical`. `scripts/github/fixtures/**` is excluded from bot review.
- CodeRabbit runs On demand: a paid round needs `@coderabbitai review --use-credits`.

## CodeRabbit round 2 (86a08606, paid $4.25)

1 Minor (the rate-limit line offered the paid step even when the carry or budget forbade a post), fixed test-first in eb370b2e.

## Proposal decisions (Dave, 2026-10-30)

`docs/self-improvement/proposals/2026-10-30-review-stack-hybrid-pr-agent.md`: D-1 to D-5 approved. In this PR: option A config (`docs/**`, `thoughts/**`, `.claude/skills/_vendor/**` skipped by both bots; CodeRabbit trivy off, CI runs it) and the D-4 'fewer, larger PRs' rule. The merge gate is a separate infra PR.

## Scope not included

- The round order uses the mutable summary `updated_at` (review-status.mjs, newestCodeRabbitRound). Tie it to commits instead. Follow-up.
- `reviews_7d_manual` refresh: it needs Dave's CSV on or after 2026-11-05 (calendar reminder set).
- The /pathway session-root limit (lane pathway-session-root).

Model + harness: claude-opus-5-5 (orchestration, Opus checks) and Sonnet kraken agents via Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0162xu8GPKraAf3vEmY7PuV8


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Review status recognizes qualifying summary-only reviews and outside-diff findings, distinguishes notices from reviews, and reports carry blockers.
  * Review carry reports merge commits and stops when the current checkout has already been reviewed.
  * Checkpoints require fresh confirmation markers, preventing previously used confirmations from being reused.
  * Comment history is read across pages; incomplete or failed reads are reported.
  * Paid-review checks provide cost and limit guidance, and indicate when approval or escalation is needed.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for review carry, confirmation markers, merge reporting, paid-review limits, and paginated comment history.

# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

@@ -267,6 +280,51 @@ Never merge the PR. That is a separate, confirmed decision. Before Dave says mer
 read the newest round in full, the fix push is verified (`review-status.mjs` on the pushed head), and the carry

+## Paid PR reviews (Dave, 2026-10-30)
+
+Billing facts (CodeRabbit docs, measured on PR #221):
+
+- A reviewed file costs $0.25.
+- Round 1 bills every reviewable PR file. A later round bills only the files changed since the last reviewed commit.
+- Billing exclusion by `path_filters` is unproven. `cr-paid.mjs` applies the filters and shows both file counts.
+- The mode is On demand. Past the included limit, a plain `@coderabbitai review` never bills.
+- A seat holder pays with `@coderabbitai review --use-credits`. It covers the current commit only.
+- In Automatic mode, an over-limit review bills with no prompt. So run the cap check before EVERY review request.
+
+Post a paid round without asking only when ALL six conditions hold:
+
+1. READY needs a CodeRabbit review of this head, and no carry is possible.
+2. The round is inside the PR round budget (`pr-checkpoint`: 1+1, risk list 1+2).
+3. The next included slot is more than 15 minutes away (comment `@coderabbitai rate limit`). Otherwise wait.
+4. The round costs $5 or less.
+5. The paid spend of all sessions today (America/Chicago date) plus this round is $15 or less.
+6. For round 2 or later: every finding of the last round is fixed, its threads are resolved, and the `cr-fix` line is clean.
+
+Stop and ask Dave when any of these is true:
+
+- The round is past the budget.
+- A fix round brings a new Major in code the fix touched (a spiral).
+- The fix since the last reviewed commit is over 30 lines or adds files.
+- Either cap would be crossed.
+- This would be the third paid round on one PR.
+
+Commands:
+
+1. Run `node scripts/github/cr-paid.mjs check --pr <N>`. It checks conditions 4 and 5, the paid round count and the fix size. It does not check conditions 1, 2, 3 and 6.
+2. On ALLOW (exit 0), post exactly the comment it prints: `@coderabbitai review --use-credits`.
+3. On ESCALATE (exit 3), stop and ask Dave. Exit 2 gives no verdict, so treat it as ESCALATE.
+4. After you post, run `node scripts/github/cr-paid.mjs record --pr <N> --head <sha> --files <K>`. It writes the shared ledger `~/.claude/state/coderabbit-paid.jsonl`.
+5. Run `node scripts/github/cr-paid.mjs today` to read today's total.
+
+Packaging rules:
+
+- Open fewer, larger PRs: bundle related work in one area into one PR (Dave, 2026-10-30).
+- Larger PRs need fewer rounds: 0 to 10 file PRs average 2.2 rounds, 26 to 60 file PRs average 1.75.
+- Round 1 bills every reviewable file, so a round 1 over 20 files goes past the $5 cap and needs Dave.
+- `docs/**`, `thoughts/**` and vendored skills are not reviewed, so they add no cost.

_doc: classes: path globs per risk class. Only ** (any number of whole path segments, also zero), * (inside one segment) and ? are special.

A glob that starts with ! is an exclusion for that class (r3 excludes eval fixtures under .claude/skills/**/evals/**). Each path gets the first class that matches it, in this order: r3, infra, steering, docs.
A path that matches no class is normal. The PR class is the highest class of any path. risk:high is never set from paths: a person adds it.
deep_enabled false: steering, infra, high and r3 PRs get review:coderabbit + review:deep-held, not review:deep (spec 4.1, Apex billing D3).
greptile.credits_used_manual: Greptile credits used this period, an integer you edit by hand. null means unknown: the router skips the u1 and u2 steps and the ledger says so.
greptile.u1_used: at or above this count, a review:deep PR gets a warning in the router comment.
greptile.u2_used: at or above this count, only r3 PRs get review:deep. Other deep classes get the held labels. Needs deep_enabled true.

greptile.u3_date: on or after this date, a deep-class PR gets one credit-check line in the router comment, but only while credits_used_manual is null. A known count means the check is done, so no line.
greptile.notify_login: GitHub login named in the u1 and u3 lines. null means nobody is pinged.
budget: CodeRabbit PR reviews per class as [opening, extra after a Major] (pr-review-loop.md 'PR review budget per class'). Read by scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.mjs. A bare number is [n, 0].

checkpoint.critical: path globs of files whose PR gets Greptile too when it is available (pr-checkpoint.mjs rule R3). A PR that touches one never takes the READY carry (review-status.mjs). Extended 2026-10-30 with the files where a fix added a real Major (.claudedocs/2026-10-30-coderabbit-rereview-study.md section 4).
checkpoint.parser: path globs of hand-written lexer and parser guards. Their PR gets one CodeRabbit review and no loop (rule R2). Dave edits this list.

checkpoint.enforce: boolean, read by the pre-pr-gate hook from the checkout the session runs in. true (live since PR D, 2026-10-29): the checkpoint rules (non-draft create, shell gh pr ready, hand review: label, self-confirm, non-literal --repo) deny the command. false (warn mode): the same commands pass and log one warn row to guard-decisions.jsonl. Only a literal true enforces. The stamp rules are enforced in both modes.

coderabbit.reviews_7d_manual: CodeRabbit PR reviews in the last 7 days, an integer Dave sets from the free '@coderabbitai rate limit' reply or the dashboard CSV export. null means unknown and changes no rule. reviews_7d_manual_date: the day Dave read it. A count older than 7 days counts as unknown.
